proposition: Let a_0 = 5, a_1 = 18 and a_n = 9*a_(n-1) + (-18)*a_(n-2) for n >= 2. Then for every n with 0 <= n <= 30, a_n = 4*3^n + 1*6^n.
hypotheses: the recurrence is applied only for n >= 2

argument.text: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, 2*n^2 is congruent to (2*n^2) + 21 modulo 7.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, if n mod 2 = 1 then (n^2) mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, at least one of the following holds: n mod 2 = 0; n mod 2 = 1.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, n^3 + 1 exceeds n^2.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, if n mod 4 = 0 then (n*(n+1)/2) mod 2 = 0.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, n^3 + n is congruent to (n^3 + n) + 133 modulo 19.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 30 for which n^3 > 15.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, at least one of the following holds: n mod 4 = 0; n mod 4 = 1; n mod 4 = 2; n mod 4 = 3.
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 30, n^3 is at least 3*n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, (n-4)*(n^2) equals (n-4)*((n^2) + [n = 4]).
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 30 for which n^2 > 15.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, (n-3)*(n^2) equals (n-3)*((n^2) + [n = 3]).
The steps above establish the statement up to 30, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 30.
